subject: Subprocessor addendum: SIG response + minimized evidence set for procurement
messages:
From: Paul Reinhart <paul.reinhart@medsys.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: vendor-security@medsys.com
Date: 2025-10-15T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: SIG intake + subprocessor list (procurement ask)

Sergio —

Thanks for the quick onboarding call today. Procurement and our security team want two things to move the PO forward:

1) A completed SIG Lite (we only need domains that touch PHI-adjacent processing)
2) A minimized subprocessor evidence bundle — specifically, a single-sheet roster + one-page attestations for any provider that handles key material or telemetry (KMS, logging, model registry, observability).

If you can provide a compact evidence set (rather than the full CAIQ dump) that lists residency (onshore/eu/apac), data categories, and whether encryption-at-rest keys are customer-controlled, that will speed review.

Can you get that to us by next week? We need to show SOC/SIG evidence in procurement by 10/24.

Thanks,
Paul
Paul Reinhart
Senior Security Program Manager, MedSys Health
paul.reinhart@medsys.com

Date: 2025-10-15T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG intake + subprocessor list (procurement ask)

Paul —

Appreciate the clear ask. We'll assemble a minimized package that meets procurement's needs. Planning to:
- Produce a single-sheet subprocessor roster (CSV/XLSX) with residency, data category scope, and KMS ownership flag.
- Produce one-page attestations for the small set of critical subprocessors (KMS, CDN logs, model registry, telemetry/observability).
- Provide a SIG-lite summary (answers to the 40-ish high-priority questions) and a short map to our SOC 2 controls for cross-reference.

Marissa — can you pull the latest roster and the attestation drafts? Jonas — can you confirm residency flags for the KMS and model registry vendors? I'll coordinate packaging and sign-off.

Sergio Alvarez
